court_record_20260802_pair.q1_regulation_inversion: Does state rate-regulation HELP retention? YES, short-run — the genuine inversion: title premium rates are state-filed/promulgated and sticky downward, so an efficiency gain is NOT competed away through price inside the rate cycle (unlike mortgage origination, where RKT's own filings show gains passed to borrowers). This makes title the thesis's best-case STRUCTURE. The cost of the inversion: visibly fat regulated margins invite (a) rate cases and (b) product removal — the FHFA waiver pilot IS the regulator attacking the pricing unit itself. Retention is a WINDOW bounded by the rate-filing cycle and the pilot's perimeter, not a perpetuity. D3 stays 1 (conditional), upgraded from pure hypothesis to 'partially printing at exactly one name (FAF)'.
